# 'Changed the football game' | Bills' special teams make all the difference in Thanksgiving Night win over the Chiefs
Nov 27, 2026 at 01:59 AM
The Buffalo Bills special teams units paved the way to a gritty 13-10 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving Night. The night featured brutal weather conditions that made points a premium, with the Bills leaning on their specialists through the final whistle.
With just four seconds left in the fourth quarter and the game tied 10-10, K Tyler Bass was called upon for a 57-yard field goal. Bass drilled the kick through the rain, wind and cold temperatures, giving his team a walkoff victory.

The game-winner was the second kick Bass made on Thursday night, with his other make coming just over three minutes into the fourth quarter to tie the game at 10-10 at the time. The 54-yarder was an important bounce back after the Bills had surrendered 10 unanswered points and lost the lead, getting them back on track.

Bass became the first kicker in NFL history with a game-tying 54+ yard field goal and a game-winning 54+ yard field goal in the fourth quarter in the same game. His 57-yarder was also the longest game-winning FG in the fourth quarter or overtime with the temperature under 35 degrees.

WR Greg Dortch was back deep to receive the punt, picking up 17 yards down to the Kansas City 39-yard line to set up the game-winning field goal. Dortch had two punt returns that went for 15 or more yards in the victory. His average field position on punt returns was the 39-yard line, compared to the Chiefs averaging the 10-yard line.

The rookie's final punt of the night helped set the Bills up for the chance to nail the game-winner, pinning the Chiefs back at their own 11-yard line.

# Bills edge Chiefs with last-second FG in low-scoring battle
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Special teams were the difference in the [Buffalo Bills](https://cdn.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/buf/buffalo-bills)' last-second Thanksgiving night win over the [Kansas City Chiefs](https://cdn.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/kc/kansas-city-chiefs). [Tyler Bass](https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/3917232/tyler-bass) drilled a 57-yard field goal as time expired at Highmark Stadium to give the Bills (10-1) a signature win, 13-10, over the Chiefs (8-3).
The field goal was set up by a tipped punt and ensuing [Greg Dortch](https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4037235/greg-dortch) return to set up the Bills in field goal range where, despite the wet and wintry conditions, Bass connected a low kick through the uprights to finish off the low-scoring affair.

Those mistakes deep in their own territory led to the Chiefs giving the ball back to the Bills. The difference in the game, one where both star quarterbacks struggled at times, was in kicker [Harrison Butker](https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/3055899/harrison-butker), who missed his field goal in the fourth quarter and Bass, who made his two attempts. The loss for the Chiefs was quite significant, as they fell to 8-3 and trail the [Denver Broncos](https://cdn.espn.com/nfl/team/_/name/den/denver-broncos) in the AFC West standings.

With six minutes left in the game, kicker [Harrison Butker](https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/3055899/harrison-butker) could have given the Chiefs a three-point lead with a 46-yard field goal. Instead, Butker continued his struggles this season, missing the kick wide right. After the kick, while the Bills and the fans roared in celebration, Butker displayed his frustration by screaming before trotting back to the sideline.
